nodes.name: Discrete singular Radon transform $T^{\mathcal{P}}$
nodes.statement: In the present article, as in \cite{iw}, we are interested in the discrete singular Radon transform $T^{\mathcal{P}}$ defined by \begin{align} T^{\mathcal{P}} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\mathbb{Z}^k\setminus\{0\}} f\big(x - \mathcal{P}(y)\big) K(y) \end{align} for a finitely supported function $f: \mathbb{Z}^{d_0} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$.

nodes.statement: To avoid some technicalities assume that $\mathcal{P}(x)=(x^d,\ldots, x)$ is a moment curve for some $d=d_0\ge2$ and $k=1$.

nodes.name: Fourier multiplier $m_n$ of $T_n^{\mathcal{P}}$ (outline)
nodes.statement: Let $m_n$ be the Fourier multiplier associated with the operator $T_n^{\mathcal{P}}$, i.e. $T_n^{\mathcal{P}}f=\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\hat f\big)$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Projections $\Xi_n$ (outline)
nodes.statement: Namely, let $\eta$ be a smooth bump function with a small support, fix $l \in \mathbb{N}$ and define for each integer $n\ge0$ the following projections \begin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_{n^l}} \eta\big(\mathcal E_n^{-1}(\xi - a/q)\big) \end{align} where $\mathcal E_n$ is a diagonal $d\times d$ matrix with positive entries $\big(\varepsilon_{j}: 1\le j\le d\big)$ such that $\varepsilon_{j}\le e^{-n^{1/5}}$ and \[ \mathscr{U}_{n^l}=\big\{a/q \in \mathbb{T}^d\cap\mathbb{Q}^d : a=(a_1, \ldots, a_d) \in \mathbb{N}^d_q \text{ and } \mathrm{gcd}(a_1, \ldots, a_d, q)=1 \text{ and } q\in P_{n^l}\big\} \] for some family $P_{n^l}$ such that $\mathbb{N}_{n^l}\subseteq P_{n^l}\subseteq \mathbb{N}_{e^{n^{1/10}}}$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.statement_short: Ξ_n is a sum of bump functions at scale E_n centred at rationals a/q with denominators in P_{n^l}.

nodes.name: Equation (1.10)
nodes.statement: \Xi_{n}(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_{n^l}} \eta\big(\mathcal E_n^{-1}(\xi - a/q)\big)
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:201

nodes.name: ℓ^p bound for the projections Ξ_n (outline)
nodes.statement: Exploiting the ideas of Ionescu and Wainger from \cite{iw}, we prove that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_{l, p}>0$ such that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_{l, p}\log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.statement_short: The projections Ξ_n are bounded on ℓ^p with norm O(log(n+2)).

nodes.name: Equation (1.11)
nodes.statement: \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_{l, p}\log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:202

nodes.name: Major/minor arc splitting (outline)
nodes.statement: Observe that \eqref{eq:201} allows us to dominate \eqref{eq:89} as follows \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_n^{\mathcal{P}}f\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_n\hat f\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} +\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_n)\hat f\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} and we can employ the ideas from the circle method of Hardy and Littlewood, which are implicit in the behaviour of the projections $\Xi_n$ and $1-\Xi_n$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Equation (1.12)
nodes.statement: \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_n^{\mathcal{P}}f\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_n\hat f\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} +\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_n)\hat f\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:91

nodes.name: Minor arc estimate (outline)
nodes.statement: Namely, the second norm on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:91} is bounded, since the multiplier $m_n(1-\Xi_n)$ is highly oscillatory. Thus appealing to \eqref{eq:202} and a variant of Weyl's inequality with logarithmic decay which has been proven in \cite{mst1}, see Theorem \ref{thm:3}, we can conclude that there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for each $n\ge0$ we have \[ \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(m_{n}(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_{ p}(n+1)^{-2}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \]
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.statement_short: The minor-arc pieces m_n(1-Ξ_n) decay like (n+1)^{-2} on ℓ^p by (1.11) and a log-decay Weyl inequality.

nodes.name: Equation (1.13)
nodes.statement: \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_n\hat f\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p}.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:32

nodes.name: Multipliers $\Delta_{n,s}^j$ (outline)
nodes.statement: For this purpose we construct new multipliers of the form \begin{align} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j}(\xi-a/q)\big)-\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j+1}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(\mathcal E_{s}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align} such that \[ \Xi_n(\xi)\simeq\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\sum_{s\ge0}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \]
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Equation (1.14)
nodes.statement: \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j}(\xi-a/q)\big)-\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j+1}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(\mathcal E_{s}(\xi-a/q)\big)
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:47

nodes.name: Square function bound for Δ_{n,s}^j (outline)
nodes.statement: Moreover, we will be able to show in Theorem \ref{thm:30}, using Theorem \ref{th:3}, that for each $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^j\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \le C_p \log(s+2) \|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} for any $s\ge0$, uniformly in $j\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.statement_short: The square function of the pieces Δ_{n,s}^j is bounded on ℓ^p with loss log(s+2), uniformly in j.

nodes.name: Equation (1.15)
nodes.statement: \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^j\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \le C_p \log(s+2) \|f\|_{\ell^p}.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:48

nodes.name: ℓ^2 decay and the Littlewood–Paley scheme (outline)
nodes.statement: Estimate \eqref{eq:48} can be thought as a discrete counterpart of the Littlewood--Paley inequality, see Theorem \ref{thm:30}. This is the key ingredient in our proof which combined with the robust $\ell^2\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ estimate \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^j\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^2} \le C2^{-\varepsilon|j|}(s+1)^{-\delta l} \|f\|_{\ell^2} \end{align} allows us to deduce \eqref{eq:32}. The last bound follows, since for each $a/q\in\mathscr{U}_{(s+1)^l}\setminus \mathscr{U}_{s^l}$ we have \[ m_{n}(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_{n}(\xi-a/q)+\mathcal O\big(2^{-n/2}\big) \] where $G(a/q)$ is the Gaussian sum and $\Phi_{n}$ is an integral counterpart of $m_{n}$, precise definitions can be found at beginning of Section \ref{sec:4}. This observation leads to \eqref{eq:49}, because $|G(a/q)|\le Cq^{-\delta}$ and $q\ge s^l$ if $a/q\in\mathscr{U}_{(s+1)^l}\setminus \mathscr{U}_{s^l}$. The decay in $|j|$ in \eqref{eq:49} follows from the assumption on the support of $\Xi_{n, s}^j$ and the behaviour of $\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)$, see Section \ref{sec:4} for more details.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.statement_short: Combining the ℓ^p square function bound with ℓ^2 decay from Gauss sum bounds gives (1.13).

nodes.name: Equation (1.16)
nodes.statement: \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^j\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^2} \le C2^{-\varepsilon|j|}(s+1)^{-\delta l} \|f\|_{\ell^2}
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:49

nodes.name: Averaging Radon operators $M_N^{\mathcal{P}}$ and truncated singular Radon transforms $T_N^{\mathcal{P}}$
nodes.statement: The ideas of exploiting projections \eqref{eq:201} have been initiated in \cite{mst1} in the context of $\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^{d_0}\big)$ boundedness of maximal functions corresponding respectively to the averaging Radon operators \begin{align} M_N^{\mathcal{P}} f(x) =N^{-k} \sum_{y\in\mathbb{N}_N^k} f\big(x-\mathcal{P}(y)\big) \end{align} where $\mathbb{N}^k_N = \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}^k$, and the truncated singular Radon transforms \begin{align} T_N^{\mathcal{P}} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\mathbb B_N\setminus\{0\}} f\big(x - \mathcal{P}(y)\big) K(y) \end{align} where $\mathbb B_N=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^k: |x|\le N\}$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Equation (1.17)
nodes.statement: M_N^{\mathcal{P}} f(x) =N^{-k} \sum_{y\in\mathbb{N}_N^k} f\big(x-\mathcal{P}(y)\big)
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:39

nodes.name: Equation (1.18)
nodes.statement: T_N^{\mathcal{P}} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\mathbb B_N\setminus\{0\}} f\big(x - \mathcal{P}(y)\big) K(y)
nodes.section: 1.1 Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.label: eq:51

nodes.name: Maximal degree $N_0$ and index set $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: We set \[ N_0 = \max\{ \deg \mathcal{P}_j : 1 \leq j \leq d_0\} \] and define the set \[ \Gamma = \big\{ \gamma \in \mathbb{Z}^k \setminus\{0\} : 0 \leq \gamma_j \leq N_0 \text{ for each } j = 1, \ldots, k \big\} \] with the lexicographic order.

nodes.name: Dimension $d$
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be the cardinality of $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Canonical polynomial mapping
nodes.statement: Next we introduce the canonical polynomial mapping $$ \mathcal{Q} = \big(\seq{\mathcal{Q}_\gamma}{\gamma \in \Gamma}\big) : \mathbb{Z}^k \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}^d $$ where $\mathcal{Q}_\gamma(x) = x^\gamma$ and $x^\gamma=x_1^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot x_k^{\gamma_k}$.

nodes.name: Matrix $A$ of anisotropic dilations
nodes.statement: Namely, let $A$ be a diagonal $d \times d$ matrix such that $$ (A v)_\gamma = \abs{\gamma} v_\gamma $$ for any $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma$, where $|\gamma|=\gamma_1+\ldots+\gamma_k$.

nodes.name: Anisotropic dilations $t^A$
nodes.statement: Then for every $t > 0$ we set $$ t^{A}=\exp(A\log t) $$ i.e. $t^A x=(t^{|\gamma|}x_{\gamma}: \gamma\in \Gamma)$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and we see that $\mathcal{Q}(tx)=t^A\mathcal{Q}(x)$.

nodes.name: Lifting map $L$ with $L\mathcal{Q}=\mathcal{P}$
nodes.statement: Observe also that each $\mathcal{P}_j$ can be expressed as $$ \mathcal{P}_j(x) = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} c_j^\gamma x^\gamma $$ for some $c_j^\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$. Moreover, the coefficients $\big(\seq{c_j^\gamma}{\gamma \in \Gamma, j \in \{1, \ldots, d_0\}}\big)$ define a linear transformation $L: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ such that $L\mathcal{Q} = \mathcal{P}$. Indeed, it is enough to set $$ (L v)_j = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} c_j^\gamma v_\gamma $$ for each $j \in \{1, \ldots, d_0\}$ and $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: ℓ^p boundedness for the canonical polynomial mapping
nodes.statement: For every $p \in (1, \infty)$ there is $C_p > 0$ such that for all $f \in \ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^{d}\big)$ \begin{align} \big\lVert T^{\mathcal{Q}} f \big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_p \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
conclusions: there is $C_p > 0$ such that
nodes.statement_short: $T^{\mathcal{Q}}$ is bounded on $\ell^p(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ for every $1<p<\infty$.
nodes.label: thm:7

nodes.name: Equation (1.19)
nodes.statement: \big\lVert T^{\mathcal{Q}} f \big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_p \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}.
nodes.label: eq:37

nodes.name: Lifting: Theorem B implies Theorem A
nodes.statement: In view of \cite[Section 11]{bigs} we can perform some lifting procedure which allows us to replace the underlying polynomial mapping $\mathcal{P}$ from \eqref{eq:35} by the canonical polynomial mapping $\mathcal{Q}$. Moreover, it shows that \eqref{eq:37} implies \eqref{eq:35} with the same constant $C_p$, see also \cite{iw} for more details. Therefore, the matters are reduced to proving \eqref{eq:37} for the canonical polynomial mapping. The advantage of working with the canonical polynomial mapping $\mathcal{Q}$ is that it has all coefficients equal to $1$, and the uniform bound in this case is immediate.
nodes.statement_short: Lifting procedure of Stein replaces P by the canonical mapping Q, so (1.19) implies (1.4) with the same constant.

nodes.name: Notation $T=T^{\mathcal{Q}}$
nodes.statement: From now on for simplicity of notation we will write $T=T^{\mathcal{Q}}$.

nodes.name: Notation $\lesssim$, $\gtrsim$
nodes.statement: If there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $A\le CB$ ($A\ge CB$) then we will write $A \lesssim B$ ($A \gtrsim B$).

nodes.name: Notation $\simeq$ and $\lesssim_\delta$
nodes.statement: Moreover, we will write $A \simeq B$ if $A \lesssim B$ and $A\gtrsim B$ hold simultaneously, and we will denote $A \lesssim_{\delta} B$ ($A \gtrsim_{\delta} B$) to indicate that the constant $C>0$ depends on some $\delta > 0$.

nodes.name: Sets $\mathbb{N}_0$ and $\mathbb{N}_N$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ and for $N \in \mathbb{N}$ we set \[ \mathbb{N}_N = \big\{1, 2, \ldots, N\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Norms $|x|_\infty$ and $|x|$
nodes.statement: For a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ we will use the following norms \[ \norm{x}_\infty = \max\{\abs{x_j} : 1 \leq j \leq d\}, \quad \text{and} \quad \norm{x} = \Big(\sum_{j = 1}^d \abs{x_j}^2\Big)^{1/2}. \]

nodes.name: Length of a multi-index
nodes.statement: If $\gamma$ is a multi-index from $\mathbb{N}_0^k$ then $\norm{\gamma} = \gamma_1 + \ldots + \gamma_k$.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^d$
nodes.statement: For a function $f \in L^1\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$ let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^d$ defined as $$ \mathcal{F} f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x) e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{x}} {\rm d}x. $$

nodes.name: Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.statement: If $f \in \ell^1\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ we set $$ \hat{f}(\xi) = \sum_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d} f(x) e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{x}}. $$

nodes.name: Inverse Fourier transform $\mathcal F^{-1}$
nodes.statement: To simplify the notation we denote by $\mathcal F^{-1}$ the inverse Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and the inverse Fourier transform on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d\equiv[0, 1)^d$ (Fourier coefficients).

nodes.name: Smooth cut-off $\eta$
nodes.statement: Let $\eta: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function such that $0 \leq \eta(x) \leq 1$ and \[ \eta(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{ for } \norm{x} \leq 1/(16 d),\\ 0 & \text{ for } \norm{x} \geq 1/(8 d). \end{cases} \]

nodes.name: η is a convolution of two bumps
nodes.statement: We will additionally assume that $\eta$ is a convolution of two non-negative smooth functions $\phi$ and $\psi$ with compact supports contained in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$.
nodes.label: rem:1

nodes.name: Parameters $N_0$, $Q_0$, $D$
nodes.statement: Let $\rho>0$ and for every $N\in\mathbb{N}$ define \[ N_0=\lfloor N^{\rho/2}\rfloor+1 \qquad \text{and} \qquad Q_0=(N_0!)^D \] where $D=D_{\rho}=\lfloor 2/\rho\rfloor+1$.

nodes.name: Primes $\mathbb P_N$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb P_N=\mathbb P\cap (N_0, N]$ where $\mathbb P$ is the set of all prime numbers.

nodes.name: Sets $\Pi(V)$ and $\Pi_k(V)$
nodes.statement: For any $V\subseteq\mathbb P_N$ we define \[ \Pi(V)=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb{N}_D}\Pi_k(V) \] where for any $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ \[ \Pi_k(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_{1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_{k}}: \ \gamma_{l}\in\mathbb{N}_D\ \text{and}\ p_{l}\in V\ \text{are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$} \big\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Π(V) is the set of products of at most D distinct primes from V, each raised to a power between 1 and D.

nodes.name: Denominator sets $P_N$
nodes.statement: Now we introduce the sets \[ P_N=\big\{q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in \Pi(\mathbb P_{N})\cup\{1\}\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Unique factorisation q = Q·w
nodes.statement: It is not difficult to see that every integer $q\in\mathbb{N}_N$ can be uniquely written as $q=Q\cdot w$ where $Q|Q_0$ and $w\in \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$.

nodes.name: Size of P_N
nodes.statement: Moreover, for sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$ we have \[q=Q\cdot w\le Q_0\cdot w\le (N_0!)^DN^{D^2}\le e^{N^{\rho}} \] thus we have $\mathbb{N}_N\subseteq P_N\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{e^{N^{\rho}}}$.
conclusions: $\mathbb{N}_N\subseteq P_N\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{e^{N^{\rho}}}$

nodes.name: Monotonicity of P_N
nodes.statement: Furthermore, if $N_1\le N_2$ then $P_{N_1}\subseteq P_{N_2}$.
conclusions: $P_{N_1}\subseteq P_{N_2}$

nodes.name: Rational sets $\mathcal R(S)$ and $A_q$
nodes.statement: For a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ we define \[ \mathcal R(S)=\big\{a/q \in \mathbb{T}^d\cap\mathbb{Q}^d : a \in A_q \text{ and } q\in S\big\} \] where for each $q\in\mathbb{N}$ \[ A_q=\big\{a\in\mathbb{N}_q^d: \mathrm{gcd}\big(q, \mathrm(a_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\big)\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Sets $\mathscr{U}_N$
nodes.statement: Finally, for each $N\in\mathbb{N}$ we will consider the sets \begin{align} \mathscr{U}_N=\mathcal R(P_N). \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (2.1)
nodes.statement: \mathscr{U}_N=\mathcal R(P_N).
nodes.label: eq:156

nodes.name: Monotonicity of U_N
nodes.statement: It is easy to see, if $N_1\le N_2$ then $\mathscr{U}_{N_1}\subseteq \mathscr{U}_{N_2}$.
conclusions: $\mathscr{U}_{N_1}\subseteq \mathscr{U}_{N_2}$

nodes.name: Θ is an L^p multiplier with bounds A_p
nodes.statement: We will assume that $\Theta$ is a multiplier on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $\mathbf{A}_p >0 $ such that for every $f\in L^2\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)\cap L^p\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\lVert\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\mathcal F f\big)\big\rVert_{L^p} \leq \mathbf{A}_p \vnorm{f}_{L^p}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (2.2)
nodes.statement: \big\lVert\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\mathcal F f\big)\big\rVert_{L^p} \leq \mathbf{A}_p \vnorm{f}_{L^p}.
nodes.label: eq:155

nodes.name: Ionescu–Wainger multipliers $\Delta_N$
nodes.statement: For each $N \in \mathbb{N}$ we define new periodic multipliers \begin{align} \Delta_N(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q) \end{align} where $\eta_N(\xi)=\eta\big(\mathcal E_N^{-1}\xi\big)$ and $\mathcal E_N$ is a diagonal $d\times d$ matrix with positive entries $(\varepsilon_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)$ such that $\varepsilon_{\gamma} \le e^{-N^{2\rho}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Δ_N sums translates Θη_N(ξ-a/q) over a/q in U_N, with η_N a bump at very small anisotropic scale E_N.

nodes.name: Equation (2.3)
nodes.statement: \Delta_N(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q)
nodes.label: eq:74

nodes.name: Ionescu–Wainger multiplier theorem with log N loss
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a multiplier on $\mathbb{R}^d$ obeying \eqref{eq:155}. Then for every $\rho>0$ and $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_{\rho, p} > 0$ such that for any $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $f \in \ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ \begin{align} \big\lVert \mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Delta_{N} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_{\rho, p} (\mathbf{A}_p+1)\log N \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
assumptions: Let $\Theta$ be a multiplier on $\mathbb{R}^d$ obeying \eqref{eq:155}.
conclusions: there is a constant $C_{\rho, p} > 0$ such that
nodes.statement_short: Periodised multiplier Δ_N built from an L^p-bounded Θ is bounded on ℓ^p(Z^d) with norm ≲ (A_p+1) log N.
nodes.label: th:3

nodes.name: Equation (2.4)
nodes.statement: \big\lVert \mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Delta_{N} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_{\rho, p} (\mathbf{A}_p+1)\log N \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}.

nodes.name: Proof plan of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{th:3} is a consequence of Theorem \ref{thm:5} and Proposition \ref{prop:5} proved below. To prove Theorem \ref{th:3} we find some $C_{\rho}>0$ and disjoint sets $\mathscr{U}_N^i\subseteq\mathscr{U}_N$ such that \[ \mathscr{U}_N=\bigcup_{1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N}\mathscr{U}_N^i \] and we show that $\Delta_N$ with the summation restricted to $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ is bounded on $\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ for every $p\in(1, \infty)$. In order to construct $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ we need a suitable partition of integers from the set $\Pi(\mathbb P_{N})\cup\{1\}$, see also \cite{iw}.
nodes.statement_short: Split U_N into C log N pieces with the O property and bound each restricted multiplier on ℓ^p.

nodes.name: $\mathcal O$ property
nodes.statement: A subset $\Lambda\subseteq \Pi(V)$ has $\mathcal O$ property if there is $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ and there are sets $S_1, S_2,\ldots, S_k$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] for each $1\le j\le k$ there is $ \beta_j\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $S_j=\{q_{j, 1},\ldots, q_{j, \beta_j}\}$; \item[(ii)] for every $q_{j, s}\in S_j$ there are $p_{j, s}\in V$ and $\gamma_j\in\mathbb{N}_D$ such that $q_{j, s}=p_{j, s}^{\gamma_j}$; \item[(iii)] for every $w\in W$ there are unique numbers $q_{1, s_1}\in S_1,\ldots, q_{k, s_k}\in S_k$ such that $w=q_{1, s_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{k, s_k}$; \item[(iv)] if $(j, s)\not=(j', s')$ then $(q_{j, s}, q_{j', s'})=1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Λ has the O property if its elements factor uniquely as products of pairwise coprime prime powers taken one from each of k sets S_1..S_k.
nodes.label: def:1

nodes.name: {1} has the O property
nodes.statement: The set $\Lambda=\{1\}$ has $\mathcal O$ property corresponding to $k=0$.

nodes.name: O property is hereditary
nodes.statement: If $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property, then each subset $\Lambda'\subseteq \Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property as well.
conclusions: each subset $\Lambda'\subseteq \Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property as well

nodes.name: Elements of an O-property set have equally many prime factors
nodes.statement: If a set $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property then each element of $\Lambda$ has the same number of prime factors $k\le D$.
conclusions: each element of $\Lambda$ has the same number of prime factors $k\le D$

nodes.name: Fundamental combinatorial lemma
nodes.statement: For every $\rho>0$ there exists a constant $C_{\rho}>0$ such that for every $N\in\mathbb{N}$ the set $\mathscr{U}_N$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_{\rho}\log N$ sets $\mathscr{U}_N^i=\mathcal R(P_N^i)$ where \begin{align} P_N^i =\big\{ q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in {\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N)\big\} \end{align} and ${\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N) \subseteq \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$ has $\mathcal O$ property for each integer $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$.
conclusions: the set $\mathscr{U}_N$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_{\rho}\log N$ sets
nodes.statement_short: U_N splits into at most C_ρ log N sets R(P_N^i) whose square-free parts Λ_i have the O property.
nodes.label: lem:12

nodes.name: Equation (2.5)
nodes.statement: P_N^i =\big\{ q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in {\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N)\big\}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement:
We have to prove that for every $V\subseteq \mathbb P_N$ the set $\Pi(V)$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$, let $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)\in\mathbb{N}_D^k$ be a multi-index and observe that \[ \Pi_k(V)= igcup_{\gamma\in\mathbb{N}_D^k}\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V) \] where \[ \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)= ig\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}:\ 	ext{$p_l\in V$ are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$}  ig\}. \] Since there are $D^k$ possible choices of exponents $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ when $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$, it only suffices to prove that every $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ can be partitioned into a union (not necessarily disjoint) of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. We claim that for each $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $C_k>0$ and a family  egin{align} \pi= ig\{\pi_i(V): 1\le i\le C_k\log |V| ig\} \end{align} of partitions of $V$ such that  egin{itemize} \item[(i)] for every $1\le i\le C_k\log |V|$ each $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}$ consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of $V$ and $V=V_1^i\cup\ldots\cup V_k^i$; \item[(ii)] for every $E\subseteq V$ with at least $k$ elements there exists $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. \end{itemize} Assume for a moment we have constructed a family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11}. Then one sees that for a fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb{N}_D^k$ we have  egin{align} \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)= igcup_{1\le i\le C_{k}\log |V|}\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V) \end{align} where \[ \Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)= ig\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}: p_{j}^{\gamma_j}\in  ig(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j} 	ext{ and $V_j^i\in\pi_i(V)$ for each $1\le j\le k$} ig\} \] and $ ig(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j}=\{p^{\gamma_j}: p\in V\cap V_j^i\} $. Indeed, the sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:28} is contained in $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ since each $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ is. For the opposite inclusion take $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ and let $E=\{p_1,\ldots, p_k\}$, then property (ii) for the family \eqref{eq:11} ensures that there is $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. Therefore, $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$. Furthermore, we see that for each $1\le i\le C_k\log N$ the sets $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ have $\mathcal O$ property. The proof will be completed if we construct the family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11} for the set $V$. We assume, for simplicity, that $V=\mathbb{N}_N$ but the result is true for all $V\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N$ containing at least $k$ elements. Now it will be more comfortable to work with surjective mappings $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto\mathbb{N}_k$ rather than with partitions of $\mathbb{N}_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. It will cause no changes to us, since every surjection $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto\mathbb{N}_k$ determines a partition $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ of $\mathbb{N}_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. For the proof we employ a probabilistic argument. Indeed, let $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto \mathbb{N}_k$ be a random surjective mapping. Assume that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_N$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}_k$ we have $\mathds{P}(\{f(n)=m\})=1/k$ independently of all other $n\in\mathbb{N}_N$. For every $E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N$ with $k$ elements we have $\mathds P(\{|f[E]|=k\})=k!/k^k$. It suffices to show that for some $r\simeq_k\log N$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ random surjections we have \[ \mathds P(\{ orall_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\ \exists _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|=k\})>0. \] In other words, for each $E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N$ with cardinality $k$ it is always possible to find, with a positive probability, among at most $C_k\log N$ random surjections at least one $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto \mathbb{N}_k$ such that $|f[E]|=k$. Then the set $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ is a partition of $\mathbb{N}_N$ and $E\cap f^{-1}[\{m\}]
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le m\le k$. The task now is the determine the exact value of $r\simeq_k\log N$. Take now $1\le r\le N$ independent random surjections $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ and observe that  egin{multline*} \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\  orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})\le \sum_{E\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N:\: |E|=k} \mathds P(\{ orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\}) \ =\sum_{E\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N:\: |E|=k} igg(1- rac{k!}{k^k} igg)^r= inom{N}{k} igg(1- rac{k!}{k^k} igg)^r \le igg( rac{eN}{k} igg)^ke^{-r rac{k!}{k^k}} =e^{k\log( rac{eN}{k})-r rac{k!}{k^k}}. \end{multline*} Therefore \[ \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\  orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})<1 \] if and only if \[ r> rac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log igg( rac{eN}{k} igg). \] Thus taking \[ r= igg\lceil rac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log igg( rac{eN}{k} igg) iggceil+1\simeq C_k\log N \] we see that it does the job. This completes the proof of Lemma ef{lem:12}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to partitioning Π_k^γ(V) via a family of C_k log N partitions of V separating every k-set. Such a family exists by a union bound over random surjections N_N→N_k.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1, part 2: reduction to (2.9)
nodes.statement: Now we can write \begin{align*} \Delta_N=\sum_{1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N}\Delta_N^i \end{align*} where for each $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$ \begin{align} \Delta_N^i(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N^i} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q) \end{align} with $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:12}. The proof of Theorem \ref{th:3} will be completed if we show that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ and $\rho>0$, there is a constant $C>0$ such that for any $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $1\le i\le C_{\rho} \log N$ we have \begin{align} \big\lVert \mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Delta_N^{i} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^{p}} \leq C (\mathbf{A}_p+1) \vnorm{f}_{\ell^{p}} \end{align} for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$.

nodes.statement: For $N \le 8^{\max\{p, p'\}/\rho}$ the bound in \eqref{eq:302} is obvious, since we allow the constant $C>0$ to depend on $p$ and $\rho$. Moreover, by the duality and interpolation, it suffices to prove \eqref{eq:302} for $p=2r$ where $r\in\mathbb{N}$. If $\Lambda=\Lambda_i(P_N)$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:12} for some $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$, then we see that $\mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda=\mathscr{U}_N^i$ and $\Delta_N^{\Lambda}=\Delta_N^i$, and consequently \eqref{eq:302} implies \eqref{eq:17} as desired.

nodes.name: Splitting of Δ_N^Λ by the denominator Q_0
nodes.statement: The function $\Theta(\xi)\eta_N(\xi)$ is regarded as a periodic function on $\mathbb{T}^d$, thus \begin{align*} \Delta_N^{\Lambda}(\xi)&=\sum_{a/q\in \mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda}\Theta(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q)\\ &= \sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}^d}\sum_{a/w\in \mathscr{W}_N}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w) \end{align*} where we have used the fact, that if $(q_1, q_2)=1$ then for every $a\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, there are unique $a_1, a_2\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, such that $a_1/q_1, a_2/q_2\in[0, 1)^d$ and \begin{align} \frac{a}{q_1q_2}=\frac{a_1}{q_1}+\frac{a_2}{q_2} \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^d}. \end{align}

nodes.statement: For any sequence $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_m})\in \mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$, let us define \[ \mathcal V_M^{\sigma}=\big\{a_{j_1, s_{j_1}}/q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}+\ldots+ a_{j_m, s_{j_m}}/q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\in\mathbb{T}^d\cap \mathbb{Q}^d: a_{j_l, s_{j_l}}\in A_{q_{j_l, s_{j_l}}}\ \text{for any}\ l\in\mathbb{N}_m\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Functions $\chi$ and $\Omega_N$
nodes.statement: Let \[ \chi(\xi)=\ind{\Lambda}(\xi) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \Omega_N(\xi)=\Theta(\xi)\eta_N(\xi). \]

nodes.name: Decomposition of Δ_N^Λ into the multipliers m_u
nodes.statement: Then again by \eqref{eq:343} we obtain \begin{multline} \Delta_N^\Lambda(\xi)= \sum_{a/w\in \mathscr{W}_N}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}^d}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\\ =\sum_{s_1\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_1}}\sum_{a_{1, s_1}\in A_{q_{1, s_1}}}\ldots\sum_{s_k\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_k}} \sum_{a_{k, s_k}\in A_{q_{k, s_k}}} m_{a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k} }(\xi)=\sum_{u\in \mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}}m_{u}(\xi) \end{multline} where \begin{align} m_{u}(\xi)=m_{a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k} }(\xi)=\chi(q_{1, s_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{k, s_k})\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}^d} \Omega_N\Big(\xi-b/Q_0-\sum_{j=1}^ka_{j, s_j}/q_{j, s_j}\Big) \end{align} for $u= a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k}$.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $\rho>0$ and $r\in\mathbb{N}$ are given. Then there is a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $N>8^{2r/\rho}$ and for any set $\Lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:300} and for every $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{u\in \mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}}f_u\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_{\rho, r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Moreover, the integer $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$, the set $\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}$ and consequently the sets $S_1,\ldots, S_k$ are determined by the set $\Lambda$ as it was described above.

nodes.name: Square functions $\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}$
nodes.statement: For any $M\subseteq \mathbb{N}_k$ and $L=\{j_1, \ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and any sequence $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l})\in \mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ let us define the following square function $\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)$ associated with the sequence $\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)$ of complex-valued functions as in \eqref{eq:25}, by setting \begin{align} \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u(x):u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)=\bigg( \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{M\setminus L}}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{L}^{\sigma}}f_{w+u+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^{1/2}, \end{align} where $M^c=\mathbb{N}_k\setminus M$.

nodes.statement: For some $s_{j_i}\in\{s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l}\}$ we will write \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u(x):u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_i}}}=\bigg(\sum_{s_{j_i}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_i}}} \big|\mathcal S_{L, M}^{(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)(x)\big|^2\bigg)^{1/2} \end{align*} which defines some function which depends on $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ and on each $s_{j_n}\in \{s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l}\}\setminus\{s_{j_i}\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there is a constant $C_r>0$ such that for any $M\subseteq\mathbb{N}_k$ and $L=\{j_1,\ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and $j_n\in M\setminus L$ and for any $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ we have \begin{align} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_r\Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \end{align} where $\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l}, s_{j_n})\in \mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_l}}\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}$ is the sequence determined by the set $L\cup\{s_{j_n}\}$. Moreover, the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:119} can be controlled in the following way \begin{multline} \Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{ s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:119} and \eqref{eq:129} can be found in \cite{mst1}. Therefore, \eqref{eq:119} combined with \eqref{eq:129} yields \begin{align} \begin{split} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}&\le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ &+C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{split} \end{align} Applying \eqref{eq:1190} recursively we obtain \begin{multline} \Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_k}\big(f_u: u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim _r \sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \mathbb{N}_k}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_{k-1}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r \sum_{s_{k-1}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}}\sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1, k\}, \mathbb{N}_k}^{(s_{k-1}, s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}+ \sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \mathbb{N}_{k}\setminus\{k-1\}}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +\sum_{s_{k-1}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1\}, \mathbb{N}_{k-1}}^{(s_{k-1})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_{k-2}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r\ldots\lesssim_{\rho, r}\sum_{\atop{M\subseteq \mathbb{N}_k}{M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}}}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}} \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:130} is completed.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: We assume, without of loss of generality, that $N\in\mathbb{N}$ is large. Let $B_h=q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\cdot Q_0\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ and observe that according to the notation from \eqref{eq:25} and \eqref{eq:13}, we have \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}= \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \le\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ =\sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \end{multline} where \begin{align} G(\xi; n, w)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}^d}\hat{f}(\xi+b/Q_0+v+w)e^{-2\pi i (b/Q_0+v)\cdot n}. \end{align} We know that for each $0<p<\infty$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\mathbb{C}^d$ we have \begin{align} \bigg(\int_{\mathbb{C}^d}|\lambda_1z_1+\ldots+\lambda_dz_d|^pe^{-\pi |z|^2} {\rm d} z\bigg)^{1/p}=C_p\big(|\lambda_1|^2+\ldots+|\lambda_d|^2\big)^{1/2}. \end{align} By Proposition 4.5 from \cite{mst1}, with the sequence of multipliers $\Theta_N=\Theta$ for all $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Theta$ as in \eqref{eq:155}, we have \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}\mathbf A_{2r} \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)} \end{align} since $\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\varepsilon_{\gamma}^{-1}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}\ge 2e^{(d+1)N^{\rho}}\ge B_h$ for sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$. Therefore, combining \eqref{eq:140} with \eqref{eq:1411} we obtain that \begin{multline} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \\=C_{2r}^{2r}\int_{\mathbb{C}^d} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\Theta\eta_N\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\int_{\mathbb{C}^d} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} \eta_NG(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:5}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: It remains to show that there exists a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $M=\{j_1,\ldots, j_m\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{k}$ any $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$ and $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}}\Big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\Big(\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-u)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big):u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\le C_{\rho, r}^{2r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Since there are $2^k$ possible choices of sets $M\subseteq \mathbb{N}_k$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ then \eqref{eq:134} will follow and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} will be completed. If $r=1$ the then Plancherel's theorem does the job since the functions $\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)$ are disjointly supported for all $b/Q_0\in \mathbb{N}_{Q_0}$, $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$, $v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}$ and $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}$. For general $r\ge2$, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\|f\|_{\ell^{2}}^2$ because we have assumed that $f$ is a characteristic function of a finite set in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, it suffices to prove for any $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} In fact, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{\infty}}=1$, it is enough to show \begin{align} \Big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^1}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any sequence of complex numbers $\big(\alpha(w): w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}\big)$ such that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2=1. \end{align} Computing the Fourier transform we obtain \begin{multline} \mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\\ =\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot w}\Big)\cdot \det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(\mathcal E_Nx\big)\cdot\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)}\Big). \end{multline} The function \begin{align} \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)} \end{align} can be written as a sum of $2^m$ functions \begin{align} \sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q)} = \begin{cases} Q^d & \mbox{if } x \equiv 0 \pmod{Q}, \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise,} \end{cases} \end{align} where possible values of $Q$ are products of $Q_0$ and $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i}$ or $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i-1}$ for $i\in\mathbb{N}_m$. Therefore, the proof of \eqref{eq:144} will be completed if we show that \begin{align} \Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot Q^d\det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^1(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any integer $Q\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ such that $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_j}$. Recall that, according Remark \ref{rem:1}, in our case $\eta=\phi*\psi$ for some two smooth functions $\phi, \psi$ supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$. Therefore, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality we only need to prove that \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\phi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} and \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} Since $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_j}$ then $Qw\not\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ for any $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$ and its denominator is bounded by $N^D$. We can assume, without of loss of generality, that $Qw\in[0, 1)^d$ by the periodicity of $x\mapsto e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}$. Inequality \eqref{eq:22} easily follows from Plancherel's theorem. In order to prove \eqref{eq:15} observe that by the change of variables one has \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)=Q^{-d}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{-1} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\psi\big(Q^{-1}\mathcal E_N^{-1}(\: \cdot-Qw) \big)\big)(x). \end{align*} Therefore, Plancherel's theorem and the last identity yield \begin{multline} Q^{d}\det(\mathcal E_N)\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}^2\\= \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\big|\psi(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}w)\big|^2{\rm d}\xi+\sum_{\atop{w_1, w_2\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}{w_1\not=w_2}}\alpha(w_1)\overline{\alpha(w_2)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\psi(\xi)\psi\big(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)\big){\rm d}\xi. \end{multline} The first sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:58} is bounded in view of \eqref{eq:50}. The second one vanishes since the function $\psi$ is supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$ and $|\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)|_{\infty}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}N^{-2D}>1$, for sufficiently large $N$. The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} is completed.

nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a polynomial in $\mathbb{R}^k$ of degree $d \in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[ P(x) = \sum_{0 < \norm{\gamma} \leq d} \xi_\gamma x^\gamma. \]

nodes.statement: Given $N \geq 1$, let $\Omega_N$ be a convex set in $\mathbb{R}^k$ such that \[ \Omega_N \subseteq \big\{x \in \mathbb{R}^k : \norm{x-x_0} \leq cN \big\} \] for some $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^k$ and $c > 0$.

nodes.statement: Assume that there is a multi-index $\gamma_0$ such that $0 < \norm{\gamma_0} \leq d$ and \[ \Big\lvert \xi_{\gamma_0} - \frac{a}{q} \Big\rvert \leq \frac{1}{q^2} \] for some integers $a, q$ such that $0\le a\le q$ and $(a, q) = 1$. nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: By Khinchine's inequality \eqref{eq:23} is equivalent to the following \begin{align} \bigg(\int_0^1\bigg\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f}\big)\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^p{\rm d}t\bigg)^{1/p}\lesssim \log N\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Observe that the multiplier from \eqref{eq:24} can be rewritten as follows \begin{align*} \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{N}}\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q) \end{align*} with the functions \[ \mathfrak m_n(\xi)=\varepsilon_n(t)\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big). \] We observe that \[ |\mathfrak m_n(\xi)|\lesssim\min\big\{|2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1}\big\}. \] The first bound follows from the mean-value theorem, since \[ \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)\big|= \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)- \Phi(0)\big|\lesssim\big|2^{nA+jI}\xi\big|\sup_{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^d}\big|\nabla \Phi(\xi)\big| \lesssim |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}. \] The second bound follows since $\Phi$ is a Schwartz function. Moreover, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is $C_p>0$ such that \[ \big\|\sup_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\mathfrak m_n\mathcal{F} f\big)\big|\big\|_{L^p}\le C_p \|f\|_{L^p} \] for every $f\in L^p\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$. Therefore, by \cite{bigs} the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi) \] corresponds to a continuous singular integral, thus defines a bounded operator on $L^p\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$ for all $p\in(1, \infty)$ with the bound independent of $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $-\infty\le M_1\le M_2\le \infty$. Hence, Theorem \ref{th:3} applies and the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi) \] defines a bounded operator on $\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ with the $\log N$ loss, and \eqref{eq:24} is established.

Theorem ef{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Xi_{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $ho>0$ from Theorem ef{th:3}. From now on we will assume that $l\in\mathbb{N}$ and $ho>0$ are related by the equation  egin{align} 10ho l=1. \end{align} Assume that $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\mapsto\mathbb{C}$ has finite support and $f\ge0$. Indeed, by Theorem ef{thm:3} we will show that for big enough $\alpha>0$, which will be specified later, and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ we have  egin{align}  ig| m_{n}(\xi)(1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)) ig|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha}. \end{align} By Dirichlet's principle we have for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q_{\gamma}|\le q_{\gamma}^{-1}n^{ eta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $1\le q_{\gamma}\le n^{- eta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Hence, taking $a'=(a_{\gamma}': \gamma\in\Gamma)$ we have $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ provided that $ eta d<l$. On the other hand, if $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)
ot=0$ then for every $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|>(16d)^{-1} 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)}. \] Therefore \[ 2^{\chi n}<16dn^{ eta} \] but this is impossible when $n\in\mathbb{N}$ is large. Hence, there is $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{ eta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{- eta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Thus by Theorem ef{thm:3} \[ |m_n(\xi)|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha} \] provided that $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)
ot=0$. This yields \eqref{eq:60} and we obtain  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^2}\lesssim(1+n)^{-\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{align} Interpolating \eqref{eq:56} with \eqref{eq:21} we obtain  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim(1+n)^{-c_p\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} for some $c_p>0$. Choosing $\alpha>0$ and $l\in\mathbb{N}$ appropriately large one obtains \eqref{eq:38}. \subsection{The estimate of the first norm in \eqref{eq:30}} Note that for any $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^d$ so that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q|\le 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)} \] for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ with $1\le q\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ we have  egin{align} m_n(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)+q^{-\delta}E_{2^n}(\xi) \end{align} where  egin{align} |E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim 2^{-n/2}. \end{align} Proposition ef{prop:0}, with $L_1=2^n$, $L_2=2^{\chi n}$ and $L_3=e^{n^{1/10}}$, establishes \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64}, since for sufficiently large $n\in\mathbb{N}$ we have \[ q^{\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim q^{\delta}L_2L_32^{-n}\lesssim  ig(e^{-n((1-\chi)\log 2-2n^{-9/10})} ig)\lesssim 2^{-n/2} \] provided $\chi>0$ is sufficiently small. Now for every $j, n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ we introduce the multipliers  egin{align} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2 \end{align} and we note that  egin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f} ig)\Big\|_{\ell^p} &\le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j<n}m_n ig(\Xi_{n}^j-\Xi_{n}^{j+1} ig)\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\ 
onumber&+\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig)\Big\|_{\ell^p}=I_p^1+I_p^2. \end{align} We will estimate $I_p^1$ and $I_p^2$ separately. For this purpose observe that by \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64} for every $a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ we have  egin{align} |m_n(\xi)|&\lesssim q^{-\delta}|\Phi_{n}(\xi-a/q)|+q^{-\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\ &\lesssim 
onumber q^{-\delta} ig(\min ig\{1, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}^{-1/d} ig\}+2^{-n/2} ig) \end{align} where the last inequality follows from \eqref{eq:18} and \eqref{eq:19}. Therefore by \eqref{eq:66} we get  egin{align}  ig|m_{n}(\xi)  ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2-\eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2 ig) ig| \lesssim q^{-\delta} ig(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2} ig). ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Observe that for any $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:63}, \eqref{eq:55} and \eqref{eq:54} we have  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\le ig\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}} M_N ig( ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig| ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For $p=2$ by Plancherel's theorem and by \eqref{eq:66} we obtain  egin{multline}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^2} =  igg(\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}|m_{n}(\xi)|^2\eta ig(2^{nA+nI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^4 |\hat{f}(\xi)|^2d\xi igg)^{1/2}\lesssim 2^{-n/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} Therefore, interpolating \eqref{eq:103} with \eqref{eq:105} we obtain for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ that  egin{align*}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align*} which in turn implies \eqref{eq:102} and $I_p^2\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$. \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^1$} Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers  egin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}} ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2 ig)\eta ig(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2 \end{align*} and we observe that by the definition \eqref{eq:69} we have  egin{align*} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}(\xi)=\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \end{align*} Moreover,  egin{multline*} \eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi) ig)^2- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi) ig)^2\ =  ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi) ig)^2- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi) ig)^2 ig) \cdot ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi) ig)- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi) ig) ig). \end{multline*} Thus we see \[ \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}(\xi)\cdot\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi), \] where  egin{align*} \Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}} ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi-a/q) ig)- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi-a/q) ig) ig)\eta ig(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q) ig) \end{align*} and  egin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}} ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2 ig)\eta ig(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q) ig). \end{align*} Moreover, $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}$ and $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 2}$ are the multipliers which satisfy the assumptions of Theorem ef{thm:30}. Therefore,  egin{multline} I_p^1=\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j< n}\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\ \le \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}\Big\|\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\ \lesssim \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\log s igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^p}. \end{multline} In the last step we have used \eqref{eq:52}. The task now is to show that for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_p>0$  egin{align}  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim s^{-2}2^{-\varepsilon j}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} This in turn will imply $I_p^1\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$ and the proof will be completed. We have assumed that $p\ge 2$, then for every $g\in\ell^r(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ such that $g\ge 0$ with $r=(p/2)'>1$ we have by \eqref{eq:63}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:55} that  egin{multline} \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig)(x) ig|^2g(x) \lesssim \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n} ig( ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig| ig)(x)^2g(x)\ \le \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n} ig( ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2 ig)(x)g(x)= \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig)(x) ig|^2 M_{2^n}^*g(x)\ \lesssim  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^p}^2  ig\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}} M_N^*g ig\|_{\ell^r} \lesssim  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^{p}}^2 \|g\|_{\ell^r}. \end{multline} Therefore, by Theorem ef{thm:30} we have  egin{align}  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log s\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} We refine the estimate in \eqref{eq:43} for $p=2$. Indeed, define \[ \varrho_{n, j}(\xi)= ig(\eta ig(2^{nA+jI}(\xi) ig)^2- \eta ig(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi) ig)^2 ig) \eta ig(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi) ig) \] and \[ \Psi_n(\xi)=\min ig\{|2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1/d}, 1 ig\}. \] By Plancherel's theorem we have  egin{multline}  igg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}} ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f} ig) ig|^2\Big)^{1/2} igg\|_{\ell^2}\ = igg(\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2|\hat f(\xi)|^2{m d}\xi igg)^{1/2}\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} The last estimate is implied by \eqref{eq:66}. Namely, by \eqref{eq:66} we may write  egin{multline} \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2\ \lesssim \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}q^{-2\delta} ig(\Psi_n(\xi-a/q)+2^{-n/2} ig) ig(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2} ig)\eta ig(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q) ig)^2\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-2\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}. \end{multline} The last line follows, since we have used the lower bound for $q\ge s^{l}$ if $a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}$. nodes.statement: We have to prove that for every $V\subseteq \mathbb P_N$ the set $\Pi(V)$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$, let $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)\in\mathbb{N}_D^k$ be a multi-index and observe that \[ \Pi_k(V)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in\mathbb{N}_D^k}\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V) \] where \[ \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}:\ \text{$p_l\in V$ are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$} \big\}. \] Since there are $D^k$ possible choices of exponents $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ when $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$, it only suffices to prove that every $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ can be partitioned into a union (not necessarily disjoint) of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property.

nodes.name: Claim: a family of C_k log |V| partitions separating every k-set suffices
nodes.statement: We claim that for each $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $C_k>0$ and a family \begin{align} \pi=\big\{\pi_i(V): 1\le i\le C_k\log |V|\big\} \end{align} of partitions of $V$ such that \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] for every $1\le i\le C_k\log |V|$ each $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}$ consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of $V$ and $V=V_1^i\cup\ldots\cup V_k^i$; \item[(ii)] for every $E\subseteq V$ with at least $k$ elements there exists $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. \end{itemize} Assume for a moment we have constructed a family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11}. Then one sees that for a fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb{N}_D^k$ we have \begin{align} \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)=\bigcup_{1\le i\le C_{k}\log |V|}\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V) \end{align} where \[ \Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}: p_{j}^{\gamma_j}\in \big(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j} \text{ and $V_j^i\in\pi_i(V)$ for each $1\le j\le k$}\big\} \] and $\big(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j}=\{p^{\gamma_j}: p\in V\cap V_j^i\} $. Indeed, the sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:28} is contained in $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ since each $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ is. For the opposite inclusion take $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ and let $E=\{p_1,\ldots, p_k\}$, then property (ii) for the family \eqref{eq:11} ensures that there is $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. Therefore, $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$. Furthermore, we see that for each $1\le i\le C_k\log N$ the sets $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ have $\mathcal O$ property.
