nodes.statement: The proof will be completed if we construct the family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11} for the set $V$. We assume, for simplicity, that $V=\mathbb{N}_N$ but the result is true for all $V\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N$ containing at least $k$ elements. Now it will be more comfortable to work with surjective mappings $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto\mathbb{N}_k$ rather than with partitions of $\mathbb{N}_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. It will cause no changes to us, since every surjection $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto\mathbb{N}_k$ determines a partition $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ of $\mathbb{N}_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulate partitions as surjections N_N → N_k

nodes.name: Introduce random surjections; reduce to positive probability of a separating family
nodes.statement: For the proof we employ a probabilistic argument. Indeed, let $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto \mathbb{N}_k$ be a random surjective mapping. Assume that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_N$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}_k$ we have $\mathds{P}(\{f(n)=m\})=1/k$ independently of all other $n\in\mathbb{N}_N$. For every $E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N$ with $k$ elements we have $\mathds P(\{|f[E]|=k\})=k!/k^k$. It suffices to show that for some $r\simeq_k\log N$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ random surjections we have \[ \mathds P(\{\forall_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\ \exists _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|=k\})>0. \] In other words, for each $E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N$ with cardinality $k$ it is always possible to find, with a positive probability, among at most $C_k\log N$ random surjections at least one $f:\mathbb{N}_N\mapsto \mathbb{N}_k$ such that $|f[E]|=k$. Then the set $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ is a partition of $\mathbb{N}_N$ and $E\cap f^{-1}[\{m\}]\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le m\le k$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce random surjections; reduce to positive probability of a separating family

nodes.name: Union bound shows r ≃ C_k log N random surjections suffice
nodes.statement: The task now is the determine the exact value of $r\simeq_k\log N$. Take now $1\le r\le N$ independent random surjections $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ and observe that \begin{multline*} \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\ \forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})\le \sum_{E\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N:\: |E|=k} \mathds P(\{\forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\}) \\ =\sum_{E\subseteq \mathbb{N}_N:\: |E|=k}\bigg(1-\frac{k!}{k^k}\bigg)^r=\binom{N}{k}\bigg(1-\frac{k!}{k^k}\bigg)^r \le\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg)^ke^{-r\frac{k!}{k^k}} =e^{k\log(\frac{eN}{k})-r\frac{k!}{k^k}}. \end{multline*} Therefore \[ \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\mathbb{N}_N}\ |E|=k\ \forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})<1 \] if and only if \[ r>\frac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg). \] Thus taking \[ r=\bigg\lceil\frac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg)\bigg\rceil+1\simeq C_k\log N \] we see that it does the job. This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:12}.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound shows r ≃ C_k log N random surjections suffice

nodes.name: Recall the square function inequalities (2.20)-(2.21) from [mst1]
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there is a constant $C_r>0$ such that for any $M\subseteq\mathbb{N}_k$ and $L=\{j_1,\ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and $j_n\in M\setminus L$ and for any $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ we have \begin{align} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_r\Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \end{align} where $\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l}, s_{j_n})\in \mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_l}}\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}$ is the sequence determined by the set $L\cup\{s_{j_n}\}$. Moreover, the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:119} can be controlled in the following way \begin{multline} \Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{ s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:119} and \eqref{eq:129} can be found in \cite{mst1}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the square function inequalities (2.20)-(2.21) from [mst1]
nodes.section: 2.2 Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Combine them into the recursive inequality (2.22)
nodes.statement: Therefore, \eqref{eq:119} combined with \eqref{eq:129} yields \begin{align} \begin{split} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}&\le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ &+C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine them into the recursive inequality (2.22)
nodes.section: 2.2 Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Iterate (2.22) over all indices to obtain (2.18)
nodes.statement: Applying \eqref{eq:1190} recursively we obtain \begin{multline} \Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_k}\big(f_u: u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim _r \sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \mathbb{N}_k}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_{k-1}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r \sum_{s_{k-1}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}}\sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1, k\}, \mathbb{N}_k}^{(s_{k-1}, s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}+ \sum_{s_{k}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \mathbb{N}_{k}\setminus\{k-1\}}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +\sum_{s_{k-1}\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1\}, \mathbb{N}_{k-1}}^{(s_{k-1})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \mathbb{N}_{k-2}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r\ldots\lesssim_{\rho, r}\sum_{\atop{M\subseteq \mathbb{N}_k}{M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}}}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}} \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:130} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate (2.22) over all indices to obtain (2.18)
nodes.section: 2.2 Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: WLOG N large
nodes.statement: We assume, without of loss of generality, that $N\in\mathbb{N}$ is large.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG N large
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Rewrite the square function along residue classes mod B_h
nodes.statement: Let $B_h=q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\cdot Q_0\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ and observe that according to the notation from \eqref{eq:25} and \eqref{eq:13}, we have \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}= \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \le\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ =\sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \end{multline} where \begin{align} G(\xi; n, w)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}^d}\hat{f}(\xi+b/Q_0+v+w)e^{-2\pi i (b/Q_0+v)\cdot n}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the square function along residue classes mod B_h
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Gaussian moment identity linearising ℓ^2 sums
nodes.statement: We know that for each $0<p<\infty$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\mathbb{C}^d$ we have \begin{align} \bigg(\int_{\mathbb{C}^d}|\lambda_1z_1+\ldots+\lambda_dz_d|^pe^{-\pi |z|^2} {\rm d} z\bigg)^{1/p}=C_p\big(|\lambda_1|^2+\ldots+|\lambda_d|^2\big)^{1/2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian moment identity linearising ℓ^2 sums
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Transfer Θ via [mst1, Prop. 4.5]
nodes.statement: By Proposition 4.5 from \cite{mst1}, with the sequence of multipliers $\Theta_N=\Theta$ for all $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Theta$ as in \eqref{eq:155}, we have \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}\mathbf A_{2r} \big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)} \end{align} since $\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\varepsilon_{\gamma}^{-1}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}\ge 2e^{(d+1)N^{\rho}}\ge B_h$ for sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer Θ via [mst1, Prop. 4.5]
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Combine to remove Θ from the square function
nodes.statement: Therefore, combining \eqref{eq:140} with \eqref{eq:1411} we obtain that \begin{multline} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \\=C_{2r}^{2r}\int_{\mathbb{C}^d} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\Theta\eta_N\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\int_{\mathbb{C}^d} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} \eta_NG(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:5}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to remove Θ from the square function
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Reduce to the bound (2.31), which yields (2.24)
nodes.statement: It remains to show that there exists a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $M=\{j_1,\ldots, j_m\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{k}$ any $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$ and $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}}\Big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\Big(\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-u)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big):u\in\mathcal U_{\mathbb{N}_k}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\le C_{\rho, r}^{2r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Since there are $2^k$ possible choices of sets $M\subseteq \mathbb{N}_k$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}_D$ then \eqref{eq:134} will follow and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} will be completed.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the bound (2.31), which yields (2.24)
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Case r=1: Plancherel and disjoint supports
nodes.statement: If $r=1$ the then Plancherel's theorem does the job since the functions $\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)$ are disjointly supported for all $b/Q_0\in \mathbb{N}_{Q_0}$, $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$, $v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}$ and $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\mathbb{N}_{\beta_{j_m}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case r=1: Plancherel and disjoint supports
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Case r≥2: reduce to a kernel ℓ^1 bound and prove it
nodes.statement: For general $r\ge2$, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\|f\|_{\ell^{2}}^2$ because we have assumed that $f$ is a characteristic function of a finite set in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, it suffices to prove for any $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} In fact, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{\infty}}=1$, it is enough to show \begin{align} \Big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^1}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any sequence of complex numbers $\big(\alpha(w): w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}\big)$ such that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2=1. \end{align} Computing the Fourier transform we obtain \begin{multline} \mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\\ =\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot w}\Big)\cdot \det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(\mathcal E_Nx\big)\cdot\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)}\Big). \end{multline} The function \begin{align} \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)} \end{align} can be written as a sum of $2^m$ functions \begin{align} \sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q)} = \begin{cases} Q^d & \mbox{if } x \equiv 0 \pmod{Q}, \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise,} \end{cases} \end{align} where possible values of $Q$ are products of $Q_0$ and $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i}$ or $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i-1}$ for $i\in\mathbb{N}_m$. Therefore, the proof of \eqref{eq:144} will be completed if we show that \begin{align} \Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot Q^d\det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^1(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any integer $Q\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ such that $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_j}$. Recall that, according Remark \ref{rem:1}, in our case $\eta=\phi*\psi$ for some two smooth functions $\phi, \psi$ supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$. Therefore, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality we only need to prove that \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\phi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} and \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} Since $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_j}$ then $Qw\not\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ for any $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$ and its denominator is bounded by $N^D$. We can assume, without of loss of generality, that $Qw\in[0, 1)^d$ by the periodicity of $x\mapsto e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}$. Inequality \eqref{eq:22} easily follows from Plancherel's theorem. In order to prove \eqref{eq:15} observe that by the change of variables one has \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)=Q^{-d}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{-1} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\psi\big(Q^{-1}\mathcal E_N^{-1}(\: \cdot-Qw) \big)\big)(x). \end{align*} Therefore, Plancherel's theorem and the last identity yield \begin{multline} Q^{d}\det(\mathcal E_N)\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}^2\\= \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\big|\psi(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}w)\big|^2{\rm d}\xi+\sum_{\atop{w_1, w_2\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}{w_1\not=w_2}}\alpha(w_1)\overline{\alpha(w_2)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\psi(\xi)\psi\big(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)\big){\rm d}\xi. \end{multline} The first sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:58} is bounded in view of \eqref{eq:50}. The second one vanishes since the function $\psi$ is supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$ and $|\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)|_{\infty}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}N^{-2D}>1$, for sufficiently large $N$. The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Case r≥2: reduce to a kernel ℓ^1 bound and prove it
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: For indicator f, reduce to the pointwise bound (2.32)
nodes.statement: For general $r\ge2$, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\|f\|_{\ell^{2}}^2$ because we have assumed that $f$ is a characteristic function of a finite set in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, it suffices to prove for any $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For indicator f, reduce to the pointwise bound (2.32)
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Dualise to the ℓ^1 bound (2.33) for normalised coefficients
nodes.statement: In fact, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{\infty}}=1$, it is enough to show \begin{align} \Big\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^1}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any sequence of complex numbers $\big(\alpha(w): w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}\big)$ such that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2=1. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Dualise to the ℓ^1 bound (2.33) for normalised coefficients
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Compute the inverse Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Computing the Fourier transform we obtain \begin{multline} \mathcal{F}^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\\ =\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot w}\Big)\cdot \det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(\mathcal E_Nx\big)\cdot\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)}\Big). \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the inverse Fourier transform
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Evaluate the exponential sums and reduce to (2.38)
nodes.statement: The function \begin{align} \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)} \end{align} can be written as a sum of $2^m$ functions \begin{align} \sum_{b\in\mathbb{N}_{Q}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q)} = \begin{cases} Q^d & \mbox{if } x \equiv 0 \pmod{Q}, \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise,} \end{cases} \end{align} where possible values of $Q$ are products of $Q_0$ and $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i}$ or $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i-1}$ for $i\in\mathbb{N}_m$. Therefore, the proof of \eqref{eq:144} will be completed if we show that \begin{align} \Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot Q^d\det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^1(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any integer $Q\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ such that $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}_{\beta_j}$.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the exponential sums and reduce to (2.38)
nodes.section: 2.3 Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.statement: In order to prove \eqref{eq:15} observe that by the change of variables one has \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)=Q^{-d}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{-1} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\psi\big(Q^{-1}\mathcal E_N^{-1}(\: \cdot-Qw) \big)\big)(x). \end{align*} Therefore, Plancherel's theorem and the last identity yield \begin{multline} Q^{d}\det(\mathcal E_N)\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}^2\\= \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\big|\psi(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}w)\big|^2{\rm d}\xi+\sum_{\atop{w_1, w_2\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}{w_1\not=w_2}}\alpha(w_1)\overline{\alpha(w_2)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\psi(\xi)\psi\big(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)\big){\rm d}\xi. \end{multline}

nodes.name: Set θ=ξ-a/q and reduce the phase mod 1 on residue classes
nodes.statement: Let $\theta = \xi - a/q$. For any $r \in \mathbb{N}_q^k$, if $y \equiv r \pmod q$ then for each $\gamma \in \Gamma$ $$ \xi_\gamma y^\gamma \equiv \theta_\gamma y^\gamma + (a_\gamma/q) r^\gamma \pmod 1, $$ thus $$ \sprod{\xi}{\mathcal{Q}(y)} \equiv \sprod{\theta}{\mathcal{Q}(y)} + \sprod{(a/q)}{\mathcal{Q}(r)} \pmod 1. $$

nodes.name: Split the sum over residues r mod q
nodes.statement: Therefore, \[ \sum_{y \in \mathbb{Z}^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\mathcal{Q}(y)}} K_n(y) = \sum_{r \in \mathbb{N}_q^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{(a/q)}{\mathcal{Q}(r)}} \sum_{y \in \mathbb{Z}^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\theta}{\mathcal{Q}(qy+r)}} K_n(qy+r). \]

nodes.name: Mean value theorem bounds for the phase and kernel
nodes.statement:
If $2^{n-2} \leq 
orm{q y + r}, 
orm{qy} \leq 2^n$ then by the mean value theorem we obtain \[  ig\lvert \sprod{	heta}{\mathcal{Q}(q y + r)} - \sprod{	heta}{\mathcal{Q}(q y)}  igvert \lesssim 
orm{r} \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \abs{	heta_\gamma} \cdot 2^{n(\abs{\gamma} - 1)} \lesssim q \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} L_1^{-\abs{\gamma}} L_2 2^{n(\abs{\gamma}-1)} \lesssim L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} ig(2^n/L_1 ig)^{\abs{\gamma}} \] and $$  ig\lvert K_n(q y + r) - K_n(q y)  igvert \lesssim 2^{-n(k+1)}L_3. $$

nodes.name: Extract G(a/q) with an explicit error

nodes.statement: Now one can replace the sum on the right-hand side by the integral. nodes.name: Khinchine's inequality: reduce to random signs
nodes.statement: By Khinchine's inequality \eqref{eq:23} is equivalent to the following \begin{align} \bigg(\int_0^1\bigg\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f}\big)\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^p{\rm d}t\bigg)^{1/p}\lesssim \log N\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Rewrite the signed multiplier
nodes.statement: Observe that the multiplier from \eqref{eq:24} can be rewritten as follows \begin{align*} \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{N}}\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q) \end{align*} with the functions \[ \mathfrak m_n(\xi)=\varepsilon_n(t)\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big). \]

nodes.name: Pointwise bounds for the pieces
nodes.statement: We observe that \[ |\mathfrak m_n(\xi)|\lesssim\min\big\{|2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1}\big\}. \] The first bound follows from the mean-value theorem, since \[ \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)\big|= \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)- \Phi(0)\big|\lesssim\big|2^{nA+jI}\xi\big|\sup_{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^d}\big|\nabla \Phi(\xi)\big| \lesssim |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}. \] The second bound follows since $\Phi$ is a Schwartz function.

nodes.name: Continuous singular integral theory gives L^p bounds
nodes.statement: Moreover, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is $C_p>0$ such that \[ \big\|\sup_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\mathfrak m_n\mathcal{F} f\big)\big|\big\|_{L^p}\le C_p \|f\|_{L^p} \] for every $f\in L^p\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$. Therefore, by \cite{bigs} the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi) \] corresponds to a continuous singular integral, thus defines a bounded operator on $L^p\big(\mathbb{R}^d\big)$ for all $p\in(1, \infty)$ with the bound independent of $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $-\infty\le M_1\le M_2\le \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuous singular integral theory gives L^p bounds

nodes.name: Theorem 1 transfers the bound to ℓ^p with log N loss
nodes.statement: Hence, Theorem \ref{th:3} applies and the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi) \] defines a bounded operator on $\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ with the $\log N$ loss, and \eqref{eq:24} is established.

nodes.name: Introduce Ξ_n, its ℓ^p bound, and split into major and minor arcs
nodes.statement: Let $\chi>0$ and $l\in\mathbb{N}$ be the numbers whose precise valued will be adjusted later. As in \cite{mst1} we will consider for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ the multipliers \begin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta\big(2^{n(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align} with $\mathscr U_{N}$ which has been defined in Section \ref{sec:6}. Theorem \ref{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $\rho>0$ from Theorem \ref{th:3}. From now on we will assume that $l\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\rho>0$ are related by the equation \begin{align} 10\rho l=1. \end{align} Assume that $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\mapsto\mathbb{C}$ has finite support and $f\ge0$. Observe that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_{n}f\Big\|_{\ell^p} \le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} + \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Without of loss of generality we may assume that $p\ge 2$, the case $1<p\le 2$ follows by the duality then.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 bounds Ξ_n on ℓ^p
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $\rho>0$ from Theorem \ref{th:3}.

nodes.statement: Assume that $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\mapsto\mathbb{C}$ has finite support and $f\ge0$. Observe that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_{n}f\Big\|_{\ell^p} \le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} + \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}

nodes.name: WLOG p≥2 by duality

nodes.name: Minor arcs: second norm in (3.18)
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim (n+1)^{-2}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For this purpose we define for every $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ the Radon averages \[ M_Nf(x)=N^{-k}\sum_{y\in\mathbb{N}_N^k}f\big(x-\mathcal{Q}(y)\big). \] From \cite{mst1} follows that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\mathbb{Z}^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}}|M_Nf|\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Then for every $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:54} and \eqref{eq:55} we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le \big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}}M_Nf\big\|_{\ell^p}+\big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}}M_N\big(\big| \mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} since we have a pointwise bound \begin{align} \big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|=|T_nf(x)|\lesssim M_{2^n}f(x). \end{align} We show that it is possible to improve estimate \eqref{eq:21} for $p=2$. Indeed, by Theorem \ref{thm:3} we will show that for big enough $\alpha>0$, which will be specified later, and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ we have \begin{align} \big| m_{n}(\xi)(1-\Xi_{n}(\xi))\big|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha}. \end{align} By Dirichlet's principle we have for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q_{\gamma}|\le q_{\gamma}^{-1}n^{\beta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $1\le q_{\gamma}\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. In order to apply Theorem \ref{thm:3} we must show that there exists some $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{\beta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Suppose for a contradiction that for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ we have $1\le q_{\gamma }<n^{\beta} $ then for some $q\le \mathrm{lcm}(q_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\le n^{\beta d}$ we have \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|\le n^{\beta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $\mathrm{gcd}\big(q, \mathrm{gcd}({a_{\gamma}'}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\big)=1$. Hence, taking $a'=(a_{\gamma}': \gamma\in\Gamma)$ we have $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ provided that $\beta d<l$. On the other hand, if $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)\not=0$ then for every $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|>(16d)^{-1} 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)}. \] Therefore \[ 2^{\chi n}<16dn^{\beta} \] but this is impossible when $n\in\mathbb{N}$ is large. Hence, there is $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{\beta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Thus by Theorem \ref{thm:3} \[ |m_n(\xi)|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha} \] provided that $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)\not=0$. This yields \eqref{eq:60} and we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2}\lesssim(1+n)^{-\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{align} Interpolating \eqref{eq:56} with \eqref{eq:21} we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim(1+n)^{-c_p\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} for some $c_p>0$. Choosing $\alpha>0$ and $l\in\mathbb{N}$ appropriately large one obtains \eqref{eq:38}.
nodes.statement_short: Minor arcs: second norm in (3.18)

nodes.name: Reduce to the decay (3.19)

nodes.name: ℓ^p bound with log(n+2) loss via the pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Then for every $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:54} and \eqref{eq:55} we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le \big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}}M_Nf\big\|_{\ell^p}+\big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}}M_N\big(\big| \mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} since we have a pointwise bound \begin{align} \big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|=|T_nf(x)|\lesssim M_{2^n}f(x). \end{align}

nodes.statement: We show that it is possible to improve estimate \eqref{eq:21} for $p=2$. Indeed, by Theorem \ref{thm:3} we will show that for big enough $\alpha>0$, which will be specified later, and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ we have \begin{align} \big| m_{n}(\xi)(1-\Xi_{n}(\xi))\big|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha}. \end{align} By Dirichlet's principle we have for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q_{\gamma}|\le q_{\gamma}^{-1}n^{\beta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $1\le q_{\gamma}\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Hence, there is $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{\beta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Thus by Theorem \ref{thm:3} \[ |m_n(\xi)|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha} \] provided that $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)\not=0$. nodes.name: Major arcs: first norm in (3.18)
nodes.statement: Note that for any $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^d$ so that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q|\le 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)} \] for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ with $1\le q\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ we have \begin{align} m_n(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)+q^{-\delta}E_{2^n}(\xi) \end{align} where \begin{align} |E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim 2^{-n/2}. \end{align} Proposition \ref{prop:0}, with $L_1=2^n$, $L_2=2^{\chi n}$ and $L_3=e^{n^{1/10}}$, establishes \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64}, since for sufficiently large $n\in\mathbb{N}$ we have \[ q^{\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim q^{\delta}L_2L_32^{-n}\lesssim \big(e^{-n((1-\chi)\log 2-2n^{-9/10})}\big)\lesssim 2^{-n/2} \] provided $\chi>0$ is sufficiently small. Now for every $j, n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ we introduce the multipliers \begin{align} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align} and we note that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} &\le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j<n}m_n\big(\Xi_{n}^j-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}\big)\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \nonumber&+\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}=I_p^1+I_p^2. \end{align} We will estimate $I_p^1$ and $I_p^2$ separately. For this purpose observe that by \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64} for every $a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ we have \begin{align} |m_n(\xi)|&\lesssim q^{-\delta}|\Phi_{n}(\xi-a/q)|+q^{-\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\\ &\lesssim \nonumber q^{-\delta}\big(\min\big\{1, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}^{-1/d}\big\}+2^{-n/2}\big) \end{align} where the last inequality follows from \eqref{eq:18} and \eqref{eq:19}. Therefore by \eqref{eq:66} we get \begin{align} \big|m_{n}(\xi) \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2-\eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\big| \lesssim q^{-\delta}\big(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2}\big). \end{align} \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^2$} It will suffice to show, for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{p}>0$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Observe that for any $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:63}, \eqref{eq:55} and \eqref{eq:54} we have \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le\big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}} M_N\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For $p=2$ by Plancherel's theorem and by \eqref{eq:66} we obtain \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2} = \bigg(\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}|m_{n}(\xi)|^2\eta\big(2^{nA+nI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^4 |\hat{f}(\xi)|^2d\xi\bigg)^{1/2}\lesssim 2^{-n/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} Therefore, interpolating \eqref{eq:103} with \eqref{eq:105} we obtain for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ that \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align*} which in turn implies \eqref{eq:102} and $I_p^2\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$. \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^1$} Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align*} and we observe that by the definition \eqref{eq:69} we have \begin{align*} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}(\xi)=\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \end{align*} Moreover, \begin{multline*} \eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\\ = \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \cdot\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi)\big)\big). \end{multline*} Thus we see \[ \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}(\xi)\cdot\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi), \] where \begin{align*} \Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big). \end{align*} Moreover, $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}$ and $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 2}$ are the multipliers which satisfy the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:30}. Therefore, \begin{multline} I_p^1=\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j< n}\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \le \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}\Big\|\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \lesssim \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\log s\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}. \end{multline} In the last step we have used \eqref{eq:52}. The task now is to show that for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_p>0$ \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim s^{-2}2^{-\varepsilon j}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} This in turn will imply $I_p^1\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$ and the proof will be completed. We have assumed that $p\ge 2$, then for every $g\in\ell^r(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ such that $g\ge 0$ with $r=(p/2)'>1$ we have by \eqref{eq:63}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:55} that \begin{multline} \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2g(x) \lesssim \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)(x)^2g(x)\\ \le \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\big)(x)g(x)= \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2 M_{2^n}^*g(x)\\ \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^2 \big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}} M_N^*g\big\|_{\ell^r} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^{p}}^2 \|g\|_{\ell^r}. \end{multline} Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm:30} we have \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log s\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} We refine the estimate in \eqref{eq:43} for $p=2$. Indeed, define \[ \varrho_{n, j}(\xi)=\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi)\big) \] and \[ \Psi_n(\xi)=\min\big\{|2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1/d}, 1\big\}. \] By Plancherel's theorem we have \begin{multline} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^2}\\ =\bigg(\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2|\hat f(\xi)|^2{\rm d}\xi\bigg)^{1/2}\\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} The last estimate is implied by \eqref{eq:66}. Namely, by \eqref{eq:66} we may write \begin{multline} \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2\\ \lesssim \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}q^{-2\delta}\big(\Psi_n(\xi-a/q)+2^{-n/2}\big)\big(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2}\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-2\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}. \end{multline} The last line follows, since we have used the lower bound for $q\ge s^{l}$ if $a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}$. Moreover, \[ \sum_{n\ge0}\big(\Psi_n(\xi-a/q)+2^{-n/2}\big)\lesssim 1 \] and \[ \sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)\lesssim 1 \] by the disjointness of the supports of $\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)$'s whenever $a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}$. Since $l\in\mathbb{N}$ can be as large as we wish thus interpolating \eqref{eq:46} with \eqref{eq:43} we obtain \eqref{eq:73} and the proof of \eqref{eq:84} and consequently Theorem \ref{thm:0} is completed.

nodes.name: Bounding I_p^1
nodes.statement: Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align*} and we observe that by the definition \eqref{eq:69} we have \begin{align*} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}(\xi)=\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \end{align*} Moreover, \begin{multline*} \eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\\ = \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \cdot\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi)\big)\big). \end{multline*} Thus we see \[ \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}(\xi)\cdot\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi), \] where \begin{align*} \Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big). \end{align*} Moreover, $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}$ and $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 2}$ are the multipliers which satisfy the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:30}. Therefore, \begin{multline} I_p^1=\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j< n}\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \le \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}\Big\|\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \lesssim \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\log s\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}. \end{multline} In the last step we have used \eqref{eq:52}. The task now is to show that for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_p>0$ \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim s^{-2}2^{-\varepsilon j}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} This in turn will imply $I_p^1\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$ and the proof will be completed. We have assumed that $p\ge 2$, then for every $g\in\ell^r(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ such that $g\ge 0$ with $r=(p/2)'>1$ we have by \eqref{eq:63}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:55} that \begin{multline} \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2g(x) \lesssim \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)(x)^2g(x)\\ \le \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\big)(x)g(x)= \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2 M_{2^n}^*g(x)\\ \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^2 \big\|\sup_{N\in\mathbb{N}} M_N^*g\big\|_{\ell^r} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^{p}}^2 \|g\|_{\ell^r}. \end{multline} Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm:30} we have \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log s\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} We refine the estimate in \eqref{eq:43} for $p=2$.
